{"role": "assistant", "content": "Pinning to v1 isn't an option either: with the override, Codex offers no multi-agent tools at all, which would break the workflow's subagents.

**Short answer:** Codex itself never encrypts handoffs. The encryption is done by the model provider, because Codex marks the `message` parameter of `spawn_agent`, `send_message` and `followup_task` as `"encrypted": true`. OpenAI's own backend honours that, which is why run 3 (signed in to ChatGPT) shows `gAAAAA…` blobs. So to get the messages into Langfuse in plaintext, the provider has to be kept from encrypting them, and Codex has to be told the reply is plaintext. Neither can be done from Codex config alone.

**What I tested.** I ran the real Codex 0.164 binary against a fake local model server, so no model was called:
- **Default setup:** the parent stores whatever the provider returned, and the child receives it in an "encrypted" field. In my fake setup that field held plain text, because nothing actually encrypted it.
- **Provider adds the plaintext marker (`encrypted_function_args: []`):** the child receives the task as ordinary readable text. This is the only route I found to plaintext.
- **Ruled out:** `features.multi_agent_v2=false` is ignored, as [openai/codex#28058](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/28058) reports. A model-name LiteLLM would pass (`zen/gpt-6.1-sol`) still gets the encrypting version. Forcing the older multi-agent version through a custom model catalog removes the subagent tools entirely.
- **Background:** [openai/codex#26210](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/26210) added the encryption, and #28058 is the open complaint that it removed the readable audit trail. [OmniRoute#14154](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/issues/14154) shows the empty-marker convention and a proxy that adds it.

**Risk for your LiteLLM plan.** If your model sits behind LiteLLM and the provider doesn't add that marker, Codex wraps each task in an "encrypted" item the backend may not understand. OmniRoute hit exactly this: subagents received no task, and the tool calls still reported success. That would quietly ruin a Codex run, independent of tracing.

**Recommended fix:** a small loopback shim between Codex and LiteLLM, started inside the sandbox by the Codex launch wrapper. It does two things:
1. On requests, it removes `"encrypted": true` from those three tools' schemas, so no provider encrypts the message.
